Green plants make their own food in the leaves by a process called photosynthesis. The plant takes in carbon dioxide from the air through tiny pores called stomata and water from the soil. The green pigment chlorophyll traps energy from sunlight. The leaf changes carbon dioxide and water into glucose and releases oxygen. Extra glucose is stored as starch.","concepts":[{"title":"Photosynthesis","summary":"Green plants make their own food in leaves using carbon dioxide, water and sunlight, producing glucose and releasing oxygen.","concept_key":"c7-science-photosynthesis"},{"title":"Stomata","summary":"Stomata are tiny pores on leaves through which plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.","concept_key":"c7-science-stomata"},{"title":"Chlorophyll","summary":"Chlorophyll is the green pigment in leaves that traps sunlight energy needed for photosynthesis.","concept_key":"c7-science-chlorophyll"},{"title":"Storage of food","summary":"Extra glucose made during photosynthesis is stored in plants as starch.","concept_key":"c7-science-starch-storage"}]}
